repositories.brief_summary: OCaml 5.5.1 shipped with Marshal/bytecode overflow fixes, while trunk got Windows Unix.select fixes and native arm64/power rounding instructions.
repositories.new_features_summary: Native arm64/power rounding instructions, Windows `Unix.select` and thread-starvation fixes, and a Haiku native backend landed on trunk.
repositories.new_features:
- POWER **assembler fix** for stack frames whose offsets exceed a 16-bit signed immediate in loads, stores, `addi`, and `li`, the POWER analogue of an earlier RISC-V fix, by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([#15021](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15021))
- Native **rounding instructions** for `Float.round`, `Float.trunc`, `ceil`, and `floor` are now emitted directly on arm64 and power instead of calling into C, by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) ([#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15017))
- Two bugs fixed in the **Win32 implementation of `Unix.select`** that could return incorrect results or fail when the same file descriptor appeared more than once across the input lists, by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) ([#15025](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15025))
- Fixed a **Windows thread-starvation bug** where an OCaml thread that never yielded voluntarily could hold the runtime lock forever, so preemptive switching between systhreads had no effect and other threads of its domain never ran, by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb), reported by [Daniel Larraz](https://github.com/daniel-larraz) ([#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15029), fixing [#15028](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15028), backported to trunk in [#15034](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15034))
- **Haiku/BeOS native-code backend** activated, with Unix socket tests and single-threaded `setlocale`/signal handling, by [Anarchos](https://github.com/Sylvain78) ([#14773](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14773))
- **Security fix**: `Marshal.data_size` now guards against integer overflow when computing `header_len + data_len` (4.14 backport), preventing objects from being read back incorrectly instead of failing cleanly, by [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy) ([#15030](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15030)) — shipped in the [OCaml 5.5.1](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/releases/tag/5.5.1) release published this week
- Fixed an **uncaught `Sys_error` exception** raised when flushing standard formatters at program exit, by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole), reported by [Olivier Andrieu](https://github.com/oandrieu) ([#15026](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15026), fixing [#14765](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14765))
- `Runtime_events.runtime_phase` gained the missing `EV_MINOR_EPHE_CLEAN` constructor for a phase the runtime has emitted since 5.4 (previously an out-of-range value crashed consumers on pattern match), and the `EV_C_MINOR_ALLOCATED_WORDS` counter now reports words of minor heap consumed including headers rather than a mismatched unit, by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([#14966](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14966), [#14969](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14969))
- KVM enabled in CI for faster Android emulator runs, by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA) ([#15003](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15003))
- GitHub issue template updated to discourage low-effort, AI-generated ("slop") bug reports, by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) ([#15031](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15031))
repositories.activity_summary: Five new unmerged PRs opened (weak.blit optimization, GADT match fix, macOS x86_64 CI retirement) alongside merged Win32 and runtime-events work.
repositories.activity:
- Newly **opened PRs** awaiting review include a `Weak.blit` optimization by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) ([#15033](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15033)), a fix to stop `lambda`/`Translcore` trusting GADT equations introduced by a partial match by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#15035](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15035)), a proposal to stop testing macOS x86_64 in CI by [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy) ([#15036](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15036)), runtime-events documentation improvements by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([#15039](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15039)), and removal of stale `opam custom-install` instructions by [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) ([#15041](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15041))
- **Windows/Win32 correctness work** dominated merges this week, with [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) landing the `Unix.select` duplicate-descriptor fix and the backup-thread starvation fix ([#15025](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15025), [#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15029), [#15034](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15034)), while [Daniel Larraz](https://github.com/daniel-larraz) followed up by opening a new report on stop-the-world barrier latency on Windows ([#15042](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15042)) and [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) opened a report of failing in-prefix tests on Windows CI ([#15040](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15040))
- **Runtime-events fixes and cleanup** from [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) closed out the missing `EV_MINOR_EPHE_CLEAN` constructor and the `minor_allocated_bytes` unit bug ([#14966](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14966), [#14969](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14969)), with the underlying ring-buffer overflow report ([#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999)) also closed; his `Domain.max_domains` proposal was closed without merging ([#14741](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14741))
- The [OCaml 5.5.1](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/releases/tag/5.5.1) point release was published by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron), bundling the `Marshal` overflow security fix ([#15030](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15030)), an earlier bytecode-loading overflow fix, a type-system bug fix for module-dependent functions, and restored cloning support on macOS
- Native-code generation continued to move work off C fallbacks, with [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) merging rounding-instruction emission for arm64/power ([#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15017)) and `fsqrt` emission for power ([#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15006)), plus opening a proposal for bit-counting C primitives with `clz`/`ctz` emitted on amd64 and arm64 that drew extensive design feedback ([#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15018))
- [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) also merged a complexity improvement for `Set.{union,inter,diff}` on sets with sharing ([#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15009))
- [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) fixed the uncaught `Sys_error` on formatter flush at exit ([#15026](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15026), closing [#14765](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14765)) and cleaned up doc comment typos ([#15038](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15038))
- [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA) merged a batch of small libunix fixes ([#14740](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14740)) and enabled KVM for faster Android emulation in CI ([#15003](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15003))
- [Anarchos](https://github.com/Sylvain78) merged activation of the Haiku native-code backend ([#14773](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14773)), while a separate Haiku native-dynlink PR was closed without merging ([#10811](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/10811))
- Other closures this week: [Aliaksei Kandratsenka](https://github.com/alk) opened a report of invalid unwind info in `ocamlopt` binaries along the stack-reallocation path ([#15037](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15037)), while races in `strstubs.c` ([#14136](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14136)) and an inline-syntax proposal for `[%foo open! struct end]` ([#13334](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13334)) were closed, and [Arthur Carcano](https://github.com/krtab)'s `caml_string_equal` optimization PR was closed without merging ([#13803](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13803))
repositories.discussions_summary: Design and security debate continued on link-time linking and bit-counting primitives, plus a timeline debate on retiring macOS x86_64 CI.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- The **link-time linking** proposal from [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust), which lets a user rewrite the compiler's linking instructions via a custom command, drew security objections from [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) about silently executing arbitrary scripts and a design critique from [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) questioning whether passing structured link information through shell-quoted environment variables can be made robust ([#14895](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14895))
- The **bit-counting primitives** PR sparked a design discussion between [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy), who separated the proposal into an uncontroversial instruction-remapping half and a more debatable new-C-primitives half (raising js_of_ocaml implementation cost), and [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp), who flagged that the C-primitive approach loses flambda constant propagation available in the current OCaml implementation ([#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15018))
- The proposal to **stop testing macOS x86_64** in CI drew pushback from [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) and [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) citing the ongoing Rosetta 2 support tail for Intel binaries, leading [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy) to instead demote the platform from tier 1 to tier 2 rather than drop it outright ([#15036](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15036))
repositories.trends_summary: Continued replacement of C fallbacks with native instructions per architecture, alongside overflow hardening and Windows-specific correctness fixes.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- **Architecture-specific native code generation** keeps replacing calls into C, spanning arm64/power rounding instructions ([#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15017)), power `fsqrt` ([#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15006)), the POWER frame-offset assembler fix ([#15021](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15021)), and the proposed bit-counting primitives ([#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15018))
- **Integer-overflow hardening** in low-level runtime paths continued, following on from the ring-buffer file-size fix ([#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000)) with the `Marshal.data_size` overflow guard that shipped in [OCaml 5.5.1](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/releases/tag/5.5.1) ([#15030](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15030))
- **Windows platform work** clustered this week, with two Win32-specific merges ([#15025](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15025), [#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15029)) and two fresh Windows-only reports opened in the same window ([#15040](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15040), [#15042](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15042))
- **CI platform tiering** is an active theme, from enabling KVM for Android emulation ([#15003](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15003)) to activating the Haiku native backend ([#14773](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14773)) to debating whether to retire macOS x86_64 ([#15036](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15036))
repositories.issues_summary: One good first issue on constructor-lookup parsing inconsistencies, with a partial-fix PR already under discussion.

repositories.brief_summary: opam 2.6.0~beta2 released with a pinning performance fix, dependency upgrades, and release-script hardening.
repositories.new_features_summary: opam 2.6.0~beta2 ships a pinning performance fix, dependency upgrades, OCaml 4.14.4 for releases, and a docs correction.
repositories.new_features:
- Bug fix for a **performance regression** where pinning a project scanned its entire directory tree recursively (including `_build` and `.git`), making `opam install --deps-only .` slow on large projects; also improved `opam update` performance by around 8% ([#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101), fixes [#7098](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7098)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- **opam 2.6.0~beta2 released** by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate), bundling the pinning performance fix together with release-checklist and reproducibility hardening ([#7115](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7115))
- Dependency **lockfile upgraded** to the latest available versions of `base64`, `spdx_licenses` (3.28.0), `menhir`, `patch`, and `checkseum`, with the OCaml compiler used for release builds bumped to 4.14.4 ([#7116](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7116))
- Install scripts (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`) updated with SHA512 checksums for the new **2.6.0~beta2** binaries across Linux, macOS, Windows, and BSD architectures ([#7119](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7119))
- Manual documentation on the **`conflicts` field** corrected to clarify that conjunctions (`&`) are disallowed between packages but allowed within filters, e.g. `"foo" {>= "3" & < "4"}`, by [Ryan Gibb](https://github.com/RyanGibb) ([#7082](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7082))
repositories.activity_summary: New draft PRs target OpamFile equality speed and Cygwin argument handling while 2.6.0~beta2 release engineering wrapped up.
repositories.activity:
- Several **new PRs opened** this week remain in draft or review: a speed-up of `OpamFile.OPAM.equal` to skip work when the two parameters are physically equal ([#7124](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7124)), a release-script simplification using `make compiler` instead of duplicating build steps ([#7121](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7121), queued on [#7120](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7120)), a fix for **empty-argument handling** in `OpamProcess.create_process_env` when invoking Cygwin binaries ([#7128](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7128), fixes [#6714](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6714)), exposing legacy `url`/`descr` file paths in `*PathName` ([#7114](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7114)), and removing duplicate directory scans plus handling removal of already-missing directories during package removal ([#7106](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7106), queued on [#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101))
- [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) reviewed [#7106](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7106) and asked for a test and changelog entry before merging
- Release engineering for **opam 2.6.0~beta2** progressed with a cleanup ensuring 32-bit release binaries have matching architectures ([#7120](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7120), split off from [#5958](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5958)), the beta2 release itself ([#7115](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7115)), and install-script checksum updates ([#7119](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7119))
- Review of the [#7082](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7082) documentation fix by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) surfaced gaps in testsuite coverage for the `conflicts` field, leading to a dedicated test PR guarding against future regressions ([#7127](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7127))
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered opam-audit security integration, depexts naming for derived distributions, and splitting lint checks by severity.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) proposed integrating **opam-audit** security-vulnerability detection directly into `opam update`/`opam install` ([#7113](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7113)); [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) questioned fetching an OCaml-specific vulnerability database in a generic package manager and pointed to the existing `--ignore-available-on` flag from [#6836](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6836)
- Ongoing debate on **depexts naming** for derived Linux distributions continued, with [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) noting a dev-meeting proposal to add separate `os-package-manager` and `os-package-repository` variables ([#4440](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/4440)), and discussion on whether `nix` or `nixos` should be the canonical `os-family` for Nix users ([#7087](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7087))
- Proposal to **split lint checks** into "important" (format errors) and "cosmetic" (missing license/description) categories, so only the former are shown during `opam install` ([#7118](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7118)), tied to inconsistent linting behavior between `opam pin add` and `opam install` ([#7117](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7117)) and a request for a `--no-lint` flag ([#7110](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7110))
- [Andriy Sultanov](https://github.com/last-genius) asked why `opam update` doesn't pick up changes to a git-hosted archive URL ([#7122](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7122)); [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) clarified this is intentional and that using a `git+https://...#branch` URL instead works as expected
repositories.trends_summary: Structured dev-meeting-driven issue triage continues alongside a steady release-engineering and performance-fix push for 2.6.0.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- **Release engineering for opam 2.6.0** dominated the week's merged work, spanning the beta2 release ([#7115](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7115)), install-script updates ([#7119](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7119)), 32-bit architecture fixes ([#7120](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7120)), and further release-script simplification queued for follow-up ([#7121](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7121))

Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) ([#7093](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7093), [#7087](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7087), [#7110](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7110), [#7105](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7105), [#4440](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/4440)), indicating a structured, recurring triage process ahead of feature decisions

repositories.brief_summary: 48 PRs merged, mostly by Rudi Grinberg, fixing rename/destruct/selection-range bugs and adding interactive construct completions.
repositories.new_features_summary: Construct completions gained interactive tab stops, plus fixes for rename, destruct-line, selection-range, and diagnostics.
repositories.new_features:
- Generated **construct completions** (e.g. `match`/`function` skeletons) are now interactive for clients with snippet support, adding tab stops so cursors can move through generated holes by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2198](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2198))
- Related diagnostic locations extracted from **Merlin's formatted messages** are now converted to zero-based LSP line numbers, fixing `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` `relatedInformation` ranges that previously pointed one line below the actual declaration by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2163](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2163), fixes [#2145](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2145))
- **Find references** now honors the client's `includeDeclaration` flag instead of always including symbol declarations in results by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2164](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2164))
- **Selection range** requests now clamp recovered ranges to document bounds and guarantee returned ranges actually contain the requested position by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2061](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2061), [#2170](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2170))
- **Destruct-line** case-analysis code actions now preserve nested or-patterns, ignore nested `with` clauses when locating cases, find match separators lexically instead of via identifier substrings, and reject malformed replies rather than crashing by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2194](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2194), [#2072](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2072), [#2043](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2043))
- **Rename** now keeps occurrence conversion on a single document snapshot to avoid inconsistent workspace edits by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2062](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2062))
- **Extract function** code action now rejects extraction when a constructor would move out of scope or resolve to a shadowing declaration by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2169](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2169))
- **Dune integration** now cleans up disconnected RPC instances, clearing stale diagnostics and promotion actions on exit without disturbing a replacement instance for the same root, and keeps promotion code-action registrations balanced when diagnostics share a source by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2189](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2189), [#2089](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2089))
- LSP request/notification handling now generates document-filter and notebook-synchronization contracts and accepts generic progress notifications by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2012](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2012), [#2166](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2166), [#2024](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2024))

repositories.brief_summary: Dune reworked dynamic actions to run over RPC and added qualified module-reference support, alongside a PR backlog cleanup.
repositories.new_features_summary: Dynamic actions now run over RPC, qualified module references are supported in per_module, and env-var precedence was fixed.
repositories.new_features:
- Dynamic actions (the `dune-action-plugin` protocol used by tools that build extra dependencies while running, such as ppxs and `dune ocaml top`) now run their **dynamic-run requests over RPC** instead of the previous ad hoc sandbox protocol, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#16256](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16256)); follow-up fixes close deadlocks and missing dependencies, populating sandboxes correctly with **dynamic dependencies** and draining in-flight requests before the sandbox is released ([#16340](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16340), [#16341](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16341), [#16342](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16342), [#16343](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16343), [#16344](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16344)).
- As part of that RPC rework, the `read_directory_with_glob` entry point moved from `Dune_action_plugin.V1` to **`Dune_rpc_lwt.V1.Action_plugin`**, a breaking change for any plugin/tool code that reads directory globs through the dynamic-action API ([#16256](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16256)).
- **Qualified module references** are now supported in fields such as `per_module` when using `(include_subdirs qualified)`, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#15633](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15633), fixes [#15578](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15578)), with a follow-up correcting generated interface module paths for **nested qualified module groups** ([#16322](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16322)) and a clearer error hint for invalid dotted module references ([#16152](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16152)).
- `(env (env-vars ...))` set in a `(context ...)` stanza of `dune-workspace` now correctly takes **precedence over the root `env` stanza**, matching the documented behavior and affecting commands such as `dune exec`, by [Puneeth Chaganti](https://github.com/punchagan) ([#16290](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16290)).
- Fixed a crash when an opam command filter is not a boolean, by [art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#16313](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16313)).
- Fixed a Melange regression where `.cmi`/`.cmt`/`.cmti` resolution failed to fall back to Melange module artifacts, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#16339](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16339)).
- Documentation for portable lock directories now cross-references the underlying joint-solver issue ([#13645](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13645)) alongside the previously-linked [#13647](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13647), by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#16315](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16315)).

- Newly opened work includes narrowing `%{bin:...}` binary lookups to a package's declared dependency closure by [Puneeth Chaganti](https://github.com/punchagan) ([#15381](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15381)), incremental clause addition for the SAT solver to support on-demand opam package loading by [art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#16303](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16303)), further opam-solver refactors splitting `build_problem` and dropping priority avoidance for `avoid-version` plus a sudoku-solving test for the SAT engine, also by [art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#16306](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16306), [#16307](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16307), [#16325](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16325)), removal of package digests by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#16292](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16292)), and `describe workspace`/`dune rules` extensions to cover Melange targets and anonymous actions by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([#16300](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16300), [#15586](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15586)).
- The **opam SAT solver** saw an incremental-solving push, with the solver refactored to expose a step/choose interface and be driven externally ([#16294](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16294)), at-most-groups made incremental ([#16304](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16304)), stats corrected to count at-most clauses ([#16293](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16293)), and a fuzzer added to check incremental solutions against brute force ([#16298](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16298)), by [art-w](https://github.com/art-w), alongside `opam_repo.load_version` exposure for single opam file reads and read-count stats ([#16297](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16297), [#16296](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16296)).
- The **qualified module references** initiative from [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) continued with encapsulated qualification validation ([#16336](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16336)), removal of unused `Per_item` from `module_name` ([#16334](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16334)), inlined common decoders in `modules` ([#16330](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16330)), and tests covering logical source paths, repeated qualified paths, and artifact reference ambiguity ([#16333](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16333), [#16321](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16321), [#16320](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16320), [#16323](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16323)); a companion documentation PR describing dotted module artifact references was opened and later closed without merging ([#16335](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16335)).
- **Melange** support was refactored to derive the emission directory from library contents, reuse library information, and reuse the emission object directory, plus preferring `melobjinfo` for imported virtual-library dependencies and isolating installed vlib fallbacks from `melobjinfo`, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#16316](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16316), [#16317](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16317), [#16318](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16318), [#16271](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16271), [#16272](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16272), [#16276](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16276), [#16277](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16277)).
- The **action-plugin/RPC** area also saw supporting refactors removing the target-writing API, merging glob handling into the action plugin, and deriving dependency comparison, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#16329](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16329), [#16328](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16328), [#16302](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16302)), plus internal `stdune` reorganisation moving `Dune_sexp` under `Stdune` ([#16288](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16288)).
- **Rocq (Coq)** support gained a test reproducing build failures from broken installed `.vo` symlinks, by [Jan-Oliver Kaiser](https://github.com/Janno) ([#16327](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16327)), tracked against an open issue proposing to ignore such symlinks when traversing installed theories ([#16326](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16326)).
- Platform-stability fixes landed for macOS (Xcode 15 C++-flag compatibility, linking test fixes, process-cleanup test stabilization) by [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder) and [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#16275](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16275), [#16274](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16274), [#16301](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16301)), and for opam promotion being restored after generated-file deletion and Merlin preferring exact configuration matches, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) and [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#16234](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16234), [#16194](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16194)).

repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered a proposed discretionary-tools stanza, per-mode linker flags, and stale compile_commands.json paths.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Sudha Parimala](https://github.com/Sudha247) posted a detailed proposal for a new `tool` stanza to declare discretionary tools in `dune-workspace`, prompting [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder) to raise questions about overloading package-specification fields with both naming and version constraints ([#16185](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16185)).
- [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) and [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) discussed whether `(env (dev (ocamlopt_flags ...)))` already covers a request for per-mode (opt vs. byte) linker flags, and whether any flags genuinely need to differ only at link time ([#16324](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16324)).
- [sully-vian](https://github.com/sully-vian) and [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) debated why Dune rewrites `directory`/`file` paths in `compile_commands.json` relative to `_build/default`, and why tools like `clangd` fail to resolve them while `ccls` copes ([#16225](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16225)).
- [Jan-Oliver Kaiser](https://github.com/Janno) reported that `--cache=disabled` still triggers unwanted recompilation making cram tests unreliable, and [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) asked for a concrete cram-stanza reproduction to narrow down the cause ([#12309](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/12309)).
- [Claudio Sacerdoti Coen](https://github.com/sacerdot) pushed back on `dune subst` silently doing nothing with `opam pin -k path` when no version can be determined, arguing the documented behavior is itself surprising for common pin workflows ([#16215](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16215)).
repositories.trends_summary: Incremental-solving groundwork in the SAT/opam solver and a backlog cleanup of stale draft PRs stood out this week.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Continued investment in making the **opam SAT solver incremental** (step/choose interface, incremental at-most groups, fuzzing against brute force) is laying groundwork for on-demand opam package loading rather than building the whole SAT problem upfront ([#16294](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16294), [#16304](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16304), [#16298](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16298), [#16303](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16303)).
- A large-scale **backlog cleanup** closed roughly two dozen long-dormant proof-of-concept and draft PRs dating back to 2022–2023 without merging, reducing open-PR clutter ([#12699](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/12699), [#12754](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/12754), [#13237](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/13237)).
- Cross-cutting **qualified module reference** work touched `include_subdirs qualified`, Melange, Menhir, and utop code paths in the same week, suggesting a coordinated refactor rather than isolated fixes ([#15633](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15633), [#16309](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16309), [#16308](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16308), [#16319](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/16319)).
- The still-open **discretionary tools** design ([#16185](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16185)) and its many linked requirement issues ([#16186](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16186)-[#16196](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16196)) show package-management tooling remains a multi-week design effort rather than a single feature.

repositories.brief_summary: Ten PRs opened tackling correctness fixes, memory/performance work, and OxCaml compatibility, with no merges landing on master during the week itself.
repositories.activity_summary: Ten new PRs opened covering resolution fixes and performance work, alongside continued long-running OxCaml feature branches.
repositories.activity:
- Ten **new PRs opened** this week by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam), covering correctness fixes to path and signature resolution: canonical chain search ([#1483](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1483)), a broken hidden-paths test ([#1484](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1484)), extended `open` support ([#1482](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1482)), module type strengthening for aliases ([#1485](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1485)), and more careful handling of strengthened signatures from includes ([#1481](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1481))
- The same author opened a set of **memory and disk usage improvements** motivated by OxCaml's `ppx_template`-heavy codebases: memoizing docstring parsing to exploit duplicate doc-comments ([#1480](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1480)), merging adjacent word tokens in parsed comments ([#1488](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1488)), and enabling **payload compression** on `.odoc`/`.odocl` files for a reported 4-5x size reduction ([#1486](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1486)); building the shape reducer once instead of repeatedly, reducing allocation, was opened and merged within the week ([#1487](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1487))
- A fix for **OCaml 5.5 compatibility** addressing incorrect rendering of optional arguments wrapped in a `TPoly` constructor was opened and merged ([#1489](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1489))
- Long-running **OxCaml feature branches** continued to receive updates: `include functor` support by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV), who incorporated an alternative desugaring from [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam)'s branch and added tests for classes, class types, and aliases ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452)); support for parameterized libraries by [art-w](https://github.com/art-w), rebased for a newer OxCaml snapshot ([#1464](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1464)); and support for kind abbreviations, also by [art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#1467](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1467))
- The **id wrapper removal** simplification, cutting disk usage by around 30% with a smaller memory reduction, was opened before the week and merged shortly after ([#1479](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1479))
- Issue [#1477](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1477), reporting that `odoc_driver` cannot find the stdlib when opam installs it under `$prefix/lib64`, was closed by [katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi) after confirming it was resolved by [#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1474)
repositories.discussions_summary: In-depth review threads on the OxCaml include-functor and parameterized-libraries PRs surfaced edge cases in module expansion and path resolution.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On the `include functor` support PR, [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) and [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) discussed a correctness concern where a generated `BODY` wrapper module needs to be re-created for each successive `include functor` application so later applications can see items produced by earlier ones, and whether values, classes, and aliases in the functor's input module are preserved correctly through expansion ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452))
- On the parameterized libraries PR, [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) raised concerns about where path resolution for instantiated libraries (`Lib[Param:Impl]` syntax) should live, preferring changes in `tools.ml` over error handling in `link.ml`, and shared a rough alternative implementation for [art-w](https://github.com/art-w) to consider; [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) contributed a round of smaller review nitpicks on spelling, dune version constraints, and code robustness ([#1464](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1464))
repositories.trends_summary: Sustained investment in reducing odoc's memory and disk footprint for OxCaml's large, comment-duplicate-heavy codebases, alongside parallel OxCaml language-feature support.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Several PRs opened this week share a common motivation: OxCaml libraries built with `ppx_template` generate large volumes of duplicated documentation comments, driving memoization ([#1480](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1480)), token-merging ([#1488](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1488)), payload compression ([#1486](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1486)), and shape-reducer sharing ([#1487](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1487)) work, following on from the id-wrapper removal merged around the same time ([#1479](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1479))
- A parallel line of work extends odoc's support for OxCaml-specific language features, with `include functor` ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452)), parameterized libraries ([#1464](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1464)), and kind abbreviations ([#1467](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1467)) all under active review
repositories.contributors_summary: Jon Ludlam opened most of the week's correctness and performance PRs and reviewed OxCaml feature work, while Marek Kubica, art-w, Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac, and katrinafyi contributed feature work, reviews, and issue triage.

repositories.discussions_summary: sahilnyk investigated the hilite.markdown CI flake and identified an unguarded fmt dependency underlying the root cause.
repositories.notable_discussions: - On [#3759](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3759), [Sahil Nayak](https://github.com/sahilnyk) investigated the proposed fix (releasing `hilite` 0.6.0 to drop the git pin) and found it may not fully resolve the flake: `hilite.markdown` is an optional dune library gated on `cmarkit`, `re`, and `fmt`, but only `cmarkit`/`re` are declared as `depopts` — `fmt` is guarded nowhere, so the markdown sublibrary can silently be skipped if `hilite` builds before `fmt` is available; they proposed moving `fmt`, `cmarkit`, and `re` into `hilite`'s real `depends` alongside the 0.6.0 release
repositories.trends_summary: Continued, now near-complete, cleanup of dead OCaml Planet feeds under the shared tracking issue, favoring disable-and-preserve-archive over deletion.

repositories.brief_summary: OCaml 5.5.1 and opam 2.6.0~beta2 landed alongside a breaking tyxml 5.0.0 release and a wave of new package submissions.
repositories.new_features_summary: OCaml 5.5.1, opam 2.6.0~beta2, a breaking tyxml 5.0.0, and several new packages including json-pointer and kube.
repositories.new_features:
- **OCaml 5.5.1** was officially published as `ocaml`, `ocaml-compiler`, `ocaml-base-compiler`, `ocaml-system`, `ocaml-src` and `ocaml-variants` by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#30637](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30637)), fixing the macOS switch-cloning failure reported in [#29496](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/29496)
- **opam 2.6.0~beta2** was published as 8 packages (`opam-core`, `opam-client`, `opam-state`, `opam-format`, `opam-solver`, `opam-repository`, `opam-installer`, `opam-devel`) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([#30603](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30603))
- CI now honours **`x-ci-accept-failures` on Windows**, recognising `msys2-mingw`/`cygwin-mingw` combinations, and the Windows regression check was tightened to only flag a failure that wasn't already failing on the base, by [Samuel Hym](https://github.com/shym) ([#28856](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/28856))
- **tyxml 5.0.0** shipped with breaking API changes by [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) ([#30641](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30641)): `hidden`/`contenteditable` now take enumerated arguments, URL-valued attributes (`a_href`, `a_ping`, etc.) go through a typed `Xml.uri`, SVG documents follow SVG 2 and drop the SVG 1.1 DTD, and several misspelled identifiers/attributes are renamed
- New package **`json-pointer`** (RFC 6901/6902/8620 JSON Pointer, Patch and JMAP wildcard support for `jsont`) by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#30656](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30656))
- New package **`kube`**, a native OCaml Kubernetes client and controller runtime, by [Ville Vesilehto](https://github.com/thevilledev) ([#30662](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30662))
- New package **`caps`**, a capability library, by [Yoann Padioleau](https://github.com/aryx) ([#30627](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30627))
- New package **`amlc-lsp`** language server by [Christopher](https://github.com/chris-in-the-shell) ([#30622](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30622))
- New package **`tdmrep`**, OCaml combinators for the W3C TDM Reservation Protocol, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#30616](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30616))
- New package **`typegist`** alongside a `jsont` 0.4.0 release, by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) ([#30614](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30614))
- New **`pidgio`** package family (`pidgio`, `pidgio-eio`, `pidgio-unix`, `pidgio-yojson`) by [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw) ([#30638](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30638))
- New **`obs-prometheus-eio`** observability backend by [Logan B. Nielsen](https://github.com/loganbnielsen) ([#30596](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30596))
- **`modelkit`** gained new `modelkit-nx` and `modelkit-talon` subpackages in its 0.4.1 release by [Clyde](https://github.com/clyde-asara) ([#30649](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30649))
- Bug fixes for the OCaml 5 runtime ABI migration: an `ocaml < 5` upper bound was added for `odbc.3.0` and `misuja`, both still calling un-prefixed `alloc_tuple`/`alloc_custom` instead of the `caml_`-prefixed versions, by [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) ([#30663](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30663), [#30661](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30661))
- Fedora 44 support was added for `conf-taglib_c.2` by [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) ([#30657](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30657))

repositories.discussions_summary: Maintainers debated automated/LLM-driven release processes, account authenticity, and archiving abandoned packages.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- Repeated fast-iterating releases from [Andreas Eldh](https://github.com/eldh)'s `matcha` package ([#30607](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30607), [#30617](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30617), [#30623](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30623)) prompted [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) to question whether a human was actually driving the account and to point out the process was adding friction for maintainers, citing the repository's [contributor-accounts policy](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/tree/master/governance/policies#14-package-contributors-accounts-should-have-a-human-behind-them)
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) raised similar concerns about [shoopeur-eng](https://github.com/shoopeur-eng)'s `realdentalcosts` package ([#30634](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30634)), noting the submitting GitHub organisation was only days old and appeared to be spraying packages across several repositories; the submitter withdrew
- [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) opened [#30550](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30550) asking whether packages whose upstream GitHub repositories have been archived should themselves be archived in opam-repository, listing dozens of candidates; [Marcello Seri](https://github.com/mseri) suggested a phased, selective approach avoiding recently-archived projects
- [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) opened [#30659](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30659) documenting recurring FreeBSD CI worker timeouts (120 minutes) even for trivial `conf-*` package installs
- On [#30587](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30587) (`yojson-bench` OCaml 4.14 constraint), [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) (the yojson maintainer) suggested dropping `yojson-bench` from opam-repository altogether since it was only published by mistake, while [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) contested that the proposed fix doesn't address the actual root cause, leaving the underlying `core_bench`/`core_unix` failure unresolved even after merge
- [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure) asked [Logan B. Nielsen](https://github.com/loganbnielsen) not to post further LLM-generated follow-up commits on `obs-eio` ([#30630](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30630)), citing shared CI resources that need to be rationed across contributors
repositories.trends_summary: Rapid iterative package releases and growing maintainer scrutiny of automated/LLM-driven submissions were the week's clearest patterns.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Several packages went through 2-3 opened-and-closed iterations within days before a working version merged, including `matcha` ([#30607](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30607), [#30617](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30617), [#30623](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30623)), `topup` ([#30562](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30562), [#30600](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30600), [#30602](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30602)), `modelkit` ([#30648](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30648), [#30649](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30649)), `kube` ([#30660](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30660), [#30662](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30662)) and `hegel` ([#30644](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30644), [#30645](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30645), [#30646](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30646))
- Maintainers ([Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm), [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure), [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust)) are increasingly pushing back on submitters whose release cadence or commit history suggests an automated or LLM-driven process without clear human oversight, invoking the repository's human-accountability policy ([#30617](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30617), [#30623](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30623), [#30630](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30630), [#30634](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30634), [#30643](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30643))
- The OCaml 5 ABI migration continues to surface old C bindings still calling un-prefixed runtime allocation functions, fixed reactively with upper bounds rather than upstream patches ([#30661](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30661), [#30663](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30663))
- The new experimental "day10" RISC-V CI pipeline is still confusing contributors and reviewers by reporting package unavailability as a hard failure rather than a skip, needing manual reassurance from [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) across multiple merges ([#30646](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30646), [#30649](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30649), [#30651](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30651), [#30656](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30656))

repositories.brief_summary: A Safari 17 code-generation bug involving the `static` keyword was reported and fixed in a same-week PR from a first-time contributor.
repositories.activity_summary: A PR was opened (and later merged) to keep `static` on the same line as the class element it modifies, fixing a Safari 17 crash.
repositories.activity:
- [habakan](https://github.com/habakan) opened [#2421](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2421), "Keep `static` on the same line as the class element it modifies," to fix [#2420](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2420) — the PR was still open at week's end and merged the following week.
- The fix targets `js_output.ml`, where `CEMethod`, `CEField`, `CEAccessor`, and `CEStaticBLock` printed `static` followed by `PP.space`, which in compact-printing mode always resolves to a newline; switching these to `PP.non_breaking_space` (matching the existing treatment of `return`, `throw`, `async`, and `using`/`await using`) keeps `static` glued to the identifier that follows it ([#2421](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2421)).
repositories.discussions_summary: The bug report diagnosed a JavaScriptCore parsing quirk on Safari 17 that misreads a line-wrapped `static` keyword as two separate class fields.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- In [#2420](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2420), [habakan](https://github.com/habakan) traced a `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'MlInt64.UNSIGNED_MAX.udivmod')` failure on Safari 17 back to generated code emitting `static` followed by a breakable line break before the field name; Safari 17's JavaScriptCore engine (unlike Node or Safari 18.5) parses `static\nNAME = ...` as a field literally named `static` followed by a separate instance field rather than as a static class field, leaving `MlInt64.UNSIGNED_MAX` undefined and breaking `Int64.of_string`.
- The report noted the bug was reproduced via a shipped artifact (`stanc.js` from `stan-dev/stanc3`) rather than a local js_of_ocaml build, and cross-referenced the ES6-compatibility discussion in [#1906](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1906) as related-but-distinct prior work on the same three `int64.js` fields.
- Discussion in [#2421](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2421) clarified that the wrapping was not occasional but occurred on every `static` class element in compact-printing mode, since `PP.space` always inserts a required separator that resolves to `\n` in that mode.
repositories.contributors_summary: First-time contributor habakan both diagnosed and fixed a Safari-specific code-generation bug in the same week.
repositories.contributors: - [habakan](https://github.com/habakan) filed [#2420](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2420) with a detailed root-cause analysis of the Safari 17 `static`-keyword line-wrapping bug, referencing the exact `js_output.ml` locations involved, and then opened [#2421](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2421) implementing the fix, noting it as their first contribution to the project and that local testing was limited by missing `xquartz`-dependent packages in their environment.

repositories.brief_summary: Atomic pointer primitives, DWARF-5 debug info, and expanded mode-polymorphism typing landed alongside continued LTO/reaper and vendoring work.
repositories.new_features_summary: New atomic pointer primitives, a -gdwarf-version flag for DWARF-5 output, [@@or_null] GADTs, and all-void block constructors.
repositories.new_features:
- New **atomic pointer primitives** (`%unsafe_atomic_load_ptr`, `%unsafe_atomic_set_ptr`, `%unsafe_atomic_exchange_ptr`, `%unsafe_atomic_cas_ptr`, `%unsafe_atomic_fetch_add_ptr`, and related operations) implemented by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([#6747](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6747)), with follow-up work avoiding an extra shift+tag when accessing fields through `idx_atomic` ([#6802](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6802)) and relaxing the `idx_atomic` kind constraint ([#6831](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6831))
- New `-gdwarf-version <4|5>` **compiler flag** selects DWARF-5 output, added by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6923](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6923)); measured on the compiler itself this cuts `.debug_loc`/`.debug_ranges` payload by roughly 26% by switching to DWARF-5 indexed location and range lists, building on the compact DWARF forms work for small constants and high PC offsets ([#6922](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6922))
- `[@@or_null]` types now support **GADTs**, including a fix for a missing partial-match warning, from [Jules Jacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) and [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6981](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6981))
- Constructors whose arguments are **all-`void`** can now be represented as statically-allocated block atoms without needing the `[@immediate_all_void_constructor]` attribute, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6880](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6880))
- Fixed an **allocation-pointer bug on stack overflow** that could corrupt recently-allocated values, and a related **C stack alignment** bug that could crash in TCMalloc, both by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) after production sightings ([#7020](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7020), [#7088](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7088))
- **Flambda2 performance work** including further n-way join improvements ([#6681](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6681)) and merging switches with many arguments that target the same destination ([#6784](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6784)), both by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp), plus allocation-free patricia-map iteration in the reaper by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6994](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6994))
- The **reaper** gained an `-Oclassic` compatibility mode, reverted and then reinstated after CI fallout, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6993](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6993), [#7067](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7067), [#7075](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7075))
- Fixed indexing of byte-element bigarrays by a truncated nativeint/int64 ([#7059](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7059)) and a jump to uninitialized data in the debugger ([#6913](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6913)), by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) and [Jack Rickard](https://github.com/Skepfyr) respectively
- `ppxlib`, `sedlex`, `js_of_ocaml` and `ocaml-compiler-libs` began being **vendored directly into the repository as subtrees** and compiled in-tree rather than pulled from opam, by [Robin Ricard](https://github.com/rricard) ([#7011](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7011), [#7014](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7014), [#7015](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7015), [#7016](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7016), [#7017](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7017), [#7018](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7018), [#7060](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7060), [#7071](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7071), [#7073](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7073), [#7074](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7074))
- Findlib/`ocamlfind` support removed from Merlin's `dot-merlin-reader`, simplifying inclusion of Merlin in the compiler distribution, by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) ([#6952](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6952))
- Bytecode magic numbers bumped to `5.4.0-ox7` ([#7019](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7019)) by [Jack Rickard](https://github.com/Skepfyr)
- New **C ABI documentation** for unboxed types and `[@unpacked]`, added by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#7046](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7046))
repositories.activity_summary: New PRs opened on LTO, metaprogramming unloading, and mode polymorphism, alongside merged work on typing internals and DWARF.
repositories.activity:
- A large batch of **new PRs opened** this week feeds ongoing threads: an LTO prototype by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([#7156](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7156)), calling-convention and slot-offset work for link-time optimization by [Miriam Vellacott](https://github.com/mirivella) ([#7030](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7030), [#6992](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6992), [#7068](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7068), [#7082](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7082)), and a series of metaprogramming/unloadable-compilation-unit PRs by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#7032](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7032), [#7033](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7033), [#7034](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7034), [#7035](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7035), [#7036](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7036), [#7037](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7037), [#7038](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7038), [#7050](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7050))
- **Mode polymorphism and modality** typing infrastructure continued to expand with new PRs from [@ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges) on mixed linking ([#7025](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7025)), curry-mode modality application ([#7056](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7056)) and printing/hiding mode-polymorphic curry modes ([#7098](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7098)), alongside [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) opening instance type constructor argument typing ([#6352](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6352)), bidirectional type checking for applications ([#6762](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6762)) and making externality a "secret" mode axis ([#7095](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7095))
- Atomics work broadened further with [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) adding atomic `ext_ptr` support ([#6937](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6937)) and refactoring index-like atomic primitive lowering ([#7047](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7047)), plus [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) opening acquire/release atomic load and store primitives ([#7048](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7048))
- [Gavin Gray](https://github.com/gavinleroy) opened a series on Merlin/compiler-artifact integration, adding module-type information to `.cms`/merlin-index artifacts ([#6801](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6801)), a `module-type-impls` query ([#6811](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6811)), synchronized Merlin import for module-type implementations ([#6872](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6872)) and annotation provenance import ([#6891](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6891))
- A **fuzzer MVP** generating random programs over a subset of OxCaml was opened by [@hwasilewskijs](https://github.com/hwasilewskijs) ([#6933](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6933)), alongside Datalog-based validators for CFG passes from the same author ([#6564](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6564), [#6673](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6673), [#7076](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7076))
- **Merged work on typing internals** included functors affected by modalities ([#5371](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5371)) and functional mode polymorphism ([#5483](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5483)) by [@ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges), middle modality mode crossing ([#6272](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6272)) and jkind normalization refactoring ([#6393](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6393)) by [Jules Jacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs), and type-directed disambiguation of `unit`/`unit#` in statements by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#6876](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6876))

repositories.brief_summary: New `Process.Env` API merged for typed environment-variable handling; Windows anonymous-pipe fix and NtCreateFile path bug opened.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `Eio.Process.Env` module adds typed environment-variable helpers (`of_bindings`, `override`, `get_opt`, `of_array`/`to_array`).
repositories.new_features:
- Added a new `Eio.Process.Env` module providing a typed representation of process environments, with `empty`, `of_bindings`, `get_opt`, `override`, `of_array` and `to_array`, replacing the raw `string array` previously used by `?env` on `Process.spawn`, `Process.run` and `Process.parse_out` ([#930](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/930)) by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5)
- `Process.Env` performs case-insensitive name comparisons on Windows while preserving the original case, following discussion between [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) about matching platform `setenv`/`execve` conventions ([#930](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/930))
- Expanded process-spawning tests in `tests/process.md`, `lib_eio_linux/tests/spawn.md` and `lib_eio_posix/test/spawn.md` to exercise the new `Env` bindings API ([#930](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/930))
repositories.activity_summary: Draft fix for Windows anonymous pipes opened by avsm; ongoing design discussion on `Eio.Vars.t` for reading environment variables without `Eio_unix`.
repositories.activity:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a draft PR fixing anonymous pipes on Windows after a `transfer` test case started failing with an `Eio.Io` exception in the pipe read path, and confirmed the failure reproduces in CI as well as locally ([#929](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/929))
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)'s earlier PR adding `Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map` remains open, with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) suggesting the helper could instead live in the submitter's own code since `Limiter` isn't exposed in the public interface ([#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/927))
- [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris)'s PR adding `Eio.Vars.t` to `Stdenv` for reading environment variables without depending on `Eio_unix` continued extensive design discussion this week, covering read-only vs. mutable environments, lazy evaluation given large environments (e.g. under Nix), naming (`get`/`get_opt`/`get_paths`), and how the module should build on the newly merged `Process.Env` ([#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923), building on [#930](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/930))
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5)'s `Process.Env` PR merged after review addressing duplicate-binding semantics, name validation, and Windows case sensitivity ([#930](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/930))
repositories.discussions_summary: Design discussion on whether Eio's process environment API should be case-insensitive and how `Eio.Vars.t` should relate to `Process.Env`.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) debated whether environment-variable name comparisons should be case-insensitive across all platforms versus only on Windows, eventually settling on Windows-only case-insensitivity plus a convention of upper-case names to keep behaviour consistent ([#930](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/930))
- Discussion on [#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923) weighed the use cases for mutating the global environment (subprocess inheritance, passing values within a process, interop with legacy `Unix`-based code) and concluded a read-only `Stdenv.vars` accessor, layered on `Process.Env`, covers most needs while avoiding `Unix.putenv` races
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura) reported that `NtCreateFile` requires fully-qualified paths on Windows, causing `Unix.ENOENT` for relative-looking paths that `Sys.file_exists` reports as present; [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) suggested adding absolute-path tests to `lib_eio_windows/test/test_fs.ml` and including the failing path in the error message, while [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) began investigating a fix involving symlink-following complexities ([#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931))
